newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-State side Tasmania humiliate Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-State side Tasmania humiliate Pakistan.

text.p: Pakistan suffered a humiliating defeat by an innings and 69 runs on Saturday after being bowled out for just 67 in their second innings on the third day of a four-day match against Tasmania.
Tasmania opener Jamie Cox had earlier scored his first double century as the state side amassed a first innings total of 435 in reply to Pakistan's opening 299.
The win was Tasmania's first over an international side since they beat India 19 years ago.
Team coach Mushtaq Mohammad was in a dark mood after the collapse and told reporters he thought his side had played poorly throughout the match.
"It was a very disappointing and dismal performance from an international side," Mushtaq said.
"We're certainly not very proud of it. We've no excuse. We just played very badly in both innings," he said.

Pakistan succumbed in the second innings without a fight as they reached 67 for nine. The innings took just 99 minutes and lasted 24.1 overs for the match to be over with a day-and-a-half of play left.
Only nine batsmen were available to Pakistan after Mohammad Zahid had stitches in a cut opened while taking a catch to dismiss former Australia batsman David Boon on Friday.
Only middle-order batsman Mohammad Wasim offered the slightest resistance and made 27 before becoming one of pace bowler John Saint's four victims.
Ijaz Ahmed with 13 was the only other batsman to reach double figures. Four batsmen -- captain Wasim Akram, openers Zahoor Elahi and Saqlain Mushtaq and Shahid Afridi -- all fell for ducks.

Saint finished with four for 10 from a remarkable bowling spell of 12 overs. All four of his wickets came without conceding a run in his final three overs. Fellow opening bowler Mark Ridgway took three for 46 from 11 overs.
Resuming at 392 for six, Tasmania held on long enough for Cox to reach exactly 200. All out 50 minutes before lunch, the home side had Pakistan reeling at 29 for four at the break.
Shortly after lunch Saint was on a hat-trick after trapping Moin Khan leg before wicket for seven and then having Wasim Akram caught at second slip with his next ball.

Mushtaq Ahmed denied Saint the hat-trick and was the last batsman out, caught by Michael DiVenuto from the first ball of all-rounder Shaun Young's second over. Young had taken seven for 64 in Pakistan's first innings.
